You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the image as a whole clearly rendered as a pencil drawing, with its visual content represented throughout in a pencil-drawn style?
node.criteria: Pass only if the image as a whole is clearly and pervasively rendered in a pencil-drawing style, with visible drawn linework and shading representing the scene rather than merely muted color, grain, or isolated sketch-like areas. Fail if it remains substantially photographic or shows only partial/ambiguous pencil-like stylization. Unknown if the visual evidence is genuinely insufficient to determine whether the whole image has been transformed.
node.binding: Compare the supplied source image with the edited image and assess the visible rendering of the scene as a whole against the requested pencil-drawing transformation; do not treat monochrome, grain, or isolated sketch-like shading alone as sufficient.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is muted and grainy, but the scene remains substantially photographic. Objects retain smooth photographic shading and texture, with no clear, pervasive pencil-drawn linework representing the scene.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s strict whole-image criterion appears to collapse meaningful but incomplete stylization into “no.” The edit is visibly desaturated and grainy, with some softened, sketch-like surface treatment, while much of the scene still reads as photographic; that supports partial progress, not completion. Keep the requirement that the whole scene become a pencil drawing, but make the decision distinguish no perceptible requested change, perceptible yet incomplete stylization, and pervasive pencil rendering. Compare source and edit for actual pencil-like marks and shading across the scene, rather than treating muted color or grain alone as sufficient. The trace is valid and queried with no dependency or transport failure, so this is a semantic calibration issue; its high confidence does not resolve the partial-versus-no boundary. Do not infer that every muted or grainy edit is partial—base the distinction on visible evidence of progress toward the requested style."}
